instructions: Finely chop the onion and the tomato. Seed and finely chop the green chili, grate 2 tsp of the ginger and chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro.
In a large bowl, stir together the 2 cups besan, 1 tsp ajwain, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 3/4 tsp salt.

Add the onion, tomato, chili, ginger and cilantro. Whisk in 1 1/3 cups water a little at a time, then up to 2/3 cup more, until the batter is thick but pours easily, like pancake batter. Add the water slowly, or the batter goes lumpy.
Set a large nonstick or cast iron pan over medium high and rub it with a few drops of the oil. Once it's hot, turn the heat down to medium.
Stir the batter up from the bottom. Pour about 1/2 cup into the middle of the pan and quickly spread it into a 6 inch round with the back of the ladle.
Drizzle about 1 tsp of oil around the edge and a few drops over the top. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges look dry and lift away from the pan.
Flip it and press the edges down with a spatula. Cook the other side for about 2 minutes, until it has golden spots and no wet batter shows when you press the middle.
Slide it onto a plate and cover it with a clean towel. Make the rest the same way, stirring the batter each time. You'll get about 8. If they brown too fast, turn the heat down a touch.
method_notes: Both versions whisk besan with ajwain and salt, stir in finely chopped onion, ginger, green chili and cilantro, and add water slowly to a thick but pourable batter that's spread thin on a hot pan turned down to medium, with oil drizzled round the edge before it's flipped and pressed. Swasthi's adds tomato and a pinch of turmeric and warns that a pan that's too hot browns them before they cook through; Cook with Manali's adds grated carrot and green pepper and cooks each side about 2 minutes. This follows Swasthi's batter at twice the amount, for about 8 chilla, with one seeded chili.
